product_one_liner.value: Luciq is an AI-powered mobile observability platform that helps mobile engineering teams detect, diagnose, prioritize, and resolve crashes, performance issues, and bugs across the app lifecycle.

employee_band.notes: Uses the published company-size band; individual employee-count estimates differ.

founded_year.notes: The company profile reports 2014; accounts of its earlier origins date back to 2012, and the company timeline describes activity before incorporation.

eng_blog.notes: Engineering posts include Khaled Elmorabea’s account of rebuilding the mobile SDK with AI and Mohamed Aziz’s account of reducing ClickHouse S3 writes, published August 24 and August 10, 2026, respectively.

public_docs.notes: Public documentation includes AI privacy, subprocessors, retention, GDPR controls, and product documentation.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: The readable board lists Enterprise Account Executive, Platform Product Manager, Senior QC Engineer, and Director of Product Marketing – Mobile Observability; none has a qualifying AI/ML/data-science title.

model_provider.notes: Listed as a subprocessor for AI-powered product features; no specific model version is asserted.

compliance_certs.notes: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 are listed as certified; HIPAA and GDPR are compliance claims, with BAA and DPA available respectively.

raised_18mo.notes: Latest identified funding round was announced May 17, 2022, before the May 9, 2025–November 9, 2026 window.

launched_6mo.notes: “AI Root Cause Analysis on Mobile: The Missing Layer Ships” announces the Crash Aggregations Engine, MCP Server, Agent Skills, Lens, and autonomous agents; page publication metadata is July 13, 2026, with a July 22 update, within the May 9–November 9 window.

leadership_change_12mo.notes: No qualifying join or departure was verified for November 9, 2025–November 9, 2026, and complete leadership-tenure coverage could not be established. Absence of an announcement is not treated as proof of no change.

crm_stack_signal.notes: The subprocessor list identifies HubSpot for marketing automation, and Salesforce.com and Totango for customer relations management.
